title: Jaemtland
capsule: Jämtland was a largely autonomous Norse-speaking republic and assembly polity in the central Scandinavian mountains, governed by the Jamtamot (a thing assembly at Frösön) and distinct from both Norway and Sweden in the early medieval period. It came under Norwegian overlordship by the late tenth century but retained substantial local self-governance. The region was ceded to Sweden by the Treaty of Roskilde in 1658, ending its Norwegian connection, though by the Cliopatria attestation window (947–1188) it was negotiating its relationship with Norwegian crown authority while preserving its thing-based republican character. Ecclesiastically it was subordinated to the archdiocese of Nidaros/Trondheim from the twelfth century onward.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The extent and political status of Jämtland in the early medieval period are poorly documented; its boundaries before Norwegian incorporation are inferred from later sources and archaeological finds rather than contemporary political records.
